title: Intrinsic finite-coefficient constructibility under nonseparated finite-type pushforward
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X,Y$ be schemes of finite type over $k$, and let $f:X	o Y$ be a $k$-morphism; separatedness is not assumed [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $B$ be a finite commutative ring and let $m\geq1$ be an integer with $mB=0$ and with $m$ invertible in $k$. Use the constant finite coefficient sheaves and the small etale and pro-etale derived categories of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], the site comparison $
u_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}	o T_{\mathrm{et}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], and ordinary total derived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Suppose $C\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},B)$ has only finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves and each is intrinsically constructible: a finite partition into locally closed constructible subschemes makes it locally constant with finite $B$-module stalks [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. Then there is $L\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and an isomorphism $
u_X^*L\cong C$. The canonical comparison gives an isomorphism $
u_Y^*Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}L\cong Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}C$, and $Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}C$ has only finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves, all intrinsically constructible. No finite Tor amplitude is assumed.
